Introduction to HTML

HTML Living Standard

HTML is the standard markup language used to create and structure content on the web. Acting as the foundational skeleton of almost every website, it instructs web browsers on how to organize and display text, images, links, and multimedia.

<h1>Learning Center</h1>
<p>Registration opens on Monday.</p>

What to expect Run the example. The browser displays Learning Center as the main heading and the registration notice below it as a paragraph.

How HTML, CSS, and JavaScript work together

Every interactive web page relies on three core layers working together. In the example below:

  • HTML builds the structure (the heading, button, and hidden notice).
  • CSS handles the styling (making the heading teal).
  • JavaScript adds interactivity (revealing the notice when you click the button).

Up next: you’ll save your own index.html file and open it directly in your browser.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Learning Center</title>
  <style>
    h1 { color: teal; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Learning Center</h1>
  <button type="button" id="show-notice">Show notice</button>
  <p id="notice" hidden>Registration opens on Monday.</p>
  <script>
    document.querySelector("#show-notice").addEventListener("click", () => {
      document.querySelector("#notice").hidden = false;
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>

What to expect The heading is teal. Click Show notice and the registration notice appears below the button.
